notes.text: Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve (ankle injury) and has missed the last 17 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Chris Kreider is out (lower-body injury), reported after he played in their last game.
Mike Matheson returned in their last game after missing 6 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 1% of the team’s shorthanded time in 12 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 18 games, up from 6% last season.

Sean Durzi is on injured reserve and has missed the last 7 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Braden Schneider has taken his spot beside Marcus Pettersson. That pair has had 55% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 103:07 together, up from 45% with Durzi.
Glenn Gawdin was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside Eeli Tolvanen and Jaroslav Chmelař.

NYR.body: The Rangers have home-ice advantage and have been out-chancing opponents lately. The Canadiens’ way back in is keeping shots to a minimum.

story.head: Fox’s favorite opponent
paras: The Rangers have won two in a row, the last a 5-1 rout of Vancouver. The Canadiens (12-3-4) beat Boston 5-2 on Thursday. Going in, the Habs are second in the Atlantic (tied for fifth in the NHL) and the Rangers third in the Metropolitan (tied for 11th).
The Canadiens’ record (.737) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.563), largely because they’re 7-5 in one-goal games. The Rangers’ record (.595) is about what their chances are worth.

The Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd), take more penalties than they draw (30th) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (29th). As for the Rangers, they get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st), lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (2nd lowest) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). The Canadiens’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Rangers. Beyond that, the Rangers’ power play (7th) could do real damage against the Canadiens’ penalty kill (23rd), though their penalty killers create chances of their own going the other way.

Cole Caufield (12 G / 6 A / 18 P in 19 GP) is tied for the Canadiens’ scoring lead, with a point in five straight games against the Rangers. Lane Hutson (3 G / 15 A / 18 P in 19 GP) shares it. For the Rangers, Adam Fox (2 G / 21 A / 23 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in eight straight games against Montréal. Alexis Lafrenière (10 G / 12 A / 22 P in 21 GP) has a team-high ten goals.
Jacob Fowler (9-1-2 / .926 SV% in 12 GS) has been a rock in net for Montréal and will likely start. Dylan Garand (7-7-1 / .910 SV% in 13 GS) is in line to start for the Rangers.
At home, Mike Sullivan likes to send Kartye, Miller and Dorofeyev out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Caufield, Suzuki and Slafkovský.

items.text: The Canadiens are newly without Chris Kreider, and have been without Ivan Demidov and Samuel Montembeault for several games. Jacob Fowler is expected to start.
Nick Suzuki has a point in six straight games against the Rangers.
The Rangers have been without Sean Durzi and Igor Shesterkin for several games. Dylan Garand is expected to start.
Juraj Slafkovský has two goals on chances worth about 6.5 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
